name: Ridge ram

baseline.name: Ridge ram
baseline.look: Shaggy blue-gray mountain herbivore with broad spiral horns.
baseline.ecology: Moves along stable ridge shelves and shelters near warm stone.
baseline.limit: Defends a narrow path when calves are nearby; not innately hostile.
baseline.encounter: Wait at marked widening points and let the herd pass.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: A ridge ram browses shelf vegetation and rests beside warm stone. Herd movement follows stable ledges rather than the shortest line across a mountain drawing.
cycle: Calves slow the group and make narrow passing places sensitive. Winter snow can cover yesterday’s widening point, requiring a fresh route inspection.
signs: Split hoof tracks converge at a ledge; torn grass and fresh droppings show recent use. A squared stance with calves behind is a boundary warning.
escalation: Watch -> block -> stamp -> short charge if trapped. Leaving an open retreat is more useful than proving dominance.
community: Frostspine guides maintain marked widening points. Travelers build time for a herd crossing into the journey rather than treating every delay as an antagonist.
scene: An urgent messenger must wait while a calf finds its footing. The cost of delay is real, but pushing past would turn one crisis into two.
motion: Broad spiral horns keep orientation; weight transfers through four legs. Use planted poses and one decisive stamp, not constant jittering fur.
sounds: Hooves, breath and ordinary herd calls. No prophetic animal voice.
rule: Mountain herbivore, not innately hostile. Calves, terrain and fatigue govern behavior; horns never become magical weapons.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
